headline: 2ND JUDGE BLOCKS
dek: U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper in Washington, D.C., blocked Trump’s August executive order: “the President cannot carve out new exceptions to birthright citizenship.”

graphic.title: WHO IS NOT A CITIZEN AT BIRTH?

items.title: DIPLOMATS’ CHILDREN
items.text: Children of foreign officials with full diplomatic immunity.

items.title: HOSTILE OCCUPIERS
items.text: Children of enemy forces in hostile occupation of U.S. territory.

items.title: FOREIGN PUBLIC SHIPS
items.text: Children born aboard foreign public ships.

items.title: INTERNATIONAL WORKERS
items.text: Parents who work for foreign governments or international organizations without diplomatic immunity.

items.title: SURROGACY, BIRTH TOURISM
items.text: Births tied to a “commercial transaction” for citizenship.

items.title: “ALIEN ENEMY” PARENTS
items.text: A parent the order labels an “alien enemy,” e.g. a designated terrorist-group member.

steps.text: Supreme Court, 6–3, strikes Trump’s first order (Trump v. Barbara)
Trump signs a second order, EO 14418
Judge Deborah Boardman (Md.) blocks it for a certified class
Judge Cooper (D.C.) blocks it for a new class of children

means.label: Who’s covered:
means.text: Cooper certified a class of children “who are or will be unlawfully denied citizenship under the Order” and barred enforcement against them while the case continues.

means.label: The administration:
means.text: The White House has said the order is consistent with the Supreme Court’s ruling. The government asked Cooper to pause any ruling pending appeal; he denied it.

means.label: Two courts:
means.text: Both rulings are preliminary. The D.C. case, Nathan v. Trump, was brought by the ACLU and allied groups.

sources: Sources: Nathan v. Trump, No. 26-cv-3377 (D.D.C.), mem. op., Nov. 25, 2026; MS NOW; The Hill; ABC News; Bloomberg Law; ACLU; CBS News and Reuters (Sept. 2 ruling, White House statement); Trump v. Barbara (June 30, 2026).
